dead.meta: Checked 2026-09-24: `.task .meta` at `app.css:134` does not appear literally anywhere in this repository's class attributes, `class:` properties, classList calls or className assignments. That supports "nothing writes it"; it does not prove that nothing sets it, because a name built at runtime is invisible to this kind of search (the one place this repository builds a class that way is the `built` entry below). Two other projects in this set have their own scoped `.meta` rules (`.ticker-tabs .meta` in Earnings-Call-Sentiment-Analyser's `docs/app.css`, `.mail .meta` in Mail-Sorter's `index.html`), so the name is a naming habit these projects share rather than something unique to this one. Where the rule came from does not change the check above; whether to delete it is a separate decision.

built.…(assembled): The eight entries above: `app.js:47` builds a class attribute from a string, with the name taken from `cls`. This line is a reminder that one class in this repository is built at runtime, so an entry under `dead` is not proof that nothing uses the name.

unstyled.wait: `app.js:172` sets `class: 'status ' + (ready ? 'ok' : slow ? 'busy' : 'wait')`; of the three states only `wait` has no rule of its own. It is not missing: the base colour of `.status i` is already the grey dot the waiting state needs (`app.css:74`), and `.status.ok i` / `.status.busy i` (`app.css:75`) only turn it green or yellow. A `.status.wait i{background:var(--text-3)}` rule would state the same value twice.
